Subject: Renewal + addendum draft (MSA + Exhibit C)

Hi Mina —

Thanks again for the conversation this morning. Attached is Caldera's preferred markup for the MSA term swap and the Exhibit C capacity schedule. Key asks from our procurement and legal teams:

- Keep the overall committed tokens at the same annual value but allow a 9-month step-up rather than an immediate uplift.
- Add a limited opt-out for a defined SLA credit if token latency exceeds SLOs for two consecutive quarters (Procurement wants clarity on operational recourse).
- Clarify data residency for embeddings stored in the cache during inference; we propose explicit language in Section 6.2.

We’ve attached Caldera-Signed-Terms-v2_redline.docx and a working Exhibit-C-Capacity-Schedule.xlsx. Can Redwood confirm which MSA clauses you’ll accept as-is, which need counter language, and whether an addendum is preferable to touching the base MSA?

Diane
Diane Park
Head of Procurement, Caldera Systems

Date: 2026-08-03T11:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal + addendum draft (MSA + Exhibit C)

Hi Diane —

Thanks for the markup and the clear asks. Quick read-through notes from our side:

- Opt-out / SLA-credit: Product & Legal prefer a remediation + credit path rather than a termination right for two consecutive quarters. We can propose a capped credit (e.g., 5% of monthly invoice for that quarter) and a playbook for root-cause review before credits are applied.
- Term sequencing: We can support the 9-month phased uplift in Exhibit C as an addendum (Addendum A) rather than changing the base MSA. That keeps historical clauses intact and simplifies signpath.
- Data residency: We need more specifics on the data types you want considered "embeddings cache"; engineering flagged that ephemeral KV cache is not the same as persisted embeddings. Suggest: precise language that distinguishes persisted embeddings from transient KV caching.

Action items from Redwood:
1) Rishi — legal redline of Caldera's doc with the credit language and addendum framing (target EOD 8/5).
2) Ben — validate Exhibit C numbers against our capacity model and provide a cost delta for the phased uplift (target 8/6).
3) Laura — prep a one-page signpath and DocuSign envelope mapping (who signs Addendum A vs base MSA).

Diane — once we push our counters, would Caldera prefer a single consolidated redline or separate files (MSA redline + Addendum A)?

Best,
Mina Haddad
Senior AM, Redwood Inference
M: +1 650 555 2048

Attachments referenced: Mutual-Action-Plan-Caldera-RDW.pdf (pdf)

Mina / team —

I pushed a redline this morning; filename: RDW_MSA_Caldera_counter_v1.docx. High-level legal changes in the redline:

- Section 3 (Term & Termination): Added explicit staged term language so Addendum A governs the phased uplift schedule. Base MSA remains a 12-mo rolling term; Addendum A specifies the phased quantities and effective dates.
- Section 6.2 (Data & Cache): Added a definition for "Transient KV Cache" (not an echo of "Persisted Embeddings") and language limiting cache residency to 30 days unless otherwise agreed.
- SLA credits: Inserted a remedial process in Section 8.4 with a credit cap of 5% per impacted month and a one-time escalation meeting requirement. Legal prefers this vs termination language.
- Insurance/Indemnity: minor housekeeping edits to align with enterprise procurement expectations — no material shifts.

I also attached an internal comment summary for the exec review. Please review and call out any commercial asks we should try to accommodate pre-counter (e.g., a one-time waivable overage in month 1 to smooth onboarding).

Rishi
Sr. Counsel, Redwood Inference

Mina / Rishi / Ben —

Appreciate the fast turn. Caldera has reviewed RDW_MSA_Caldera_counter_v1.docx and Tom sent a short legal note (inline) — overall Caldera is comfortable with the Addendum approach but requests the following final items before we move to signatures:

1) Explicit callout in Addendum A that the phased uplift months are non-cumulative (Caldera's finance wants to avoid auto-billing for unused burst in month 2).
2) Confirm the KV cache residency cap (30 days) applies only to non-production embeddings generated via the platform; we will confirm a short list of artifact types.
3) A one-time onboarding overage credit (first 30 days) capped at $10k to offset migration spikes — this is commercial, not legal.

If Redwood can accept 1 & 2 in a final pass and route 3 for commercial approval, we can prepare DocuSign with parallel signers: Caldera CFO and Redwood Legal. Target: sign by 8/18 to keep the renewal effective 9/1.

Thanks —
Diane
